Galatasaray forward, Rafael Leão, has thanked Nigerian striker, Victor Osimhen, for allowing him to take a penalty during the club’s 4-0 victory over Konyaspor in the Turkish Super Lig on Friday. Leão scored his first goal for the Turkish champions after Osimhen handed him the opportunity to convert a second-half spot-kick, despite being the club’s regular penalty taker. The gesture came a day after Osimhen and his partner welcomed their second daughter, Liora Audrey, on Thursday. Osimhen had earlier opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a header, dedicating the goal to his newborn daughter through his celebration. Speaking after the match on Galatasaray’s official YouTube channel, Leão revealed that he had encouraged the Nigerian striker to score twice in celebration of the birth of his child. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Yesterday was the birth of his second child. So I told him, ‘You should score two goals today.’ He could have scored the second goal, but he gave me the ball,” the Portuguese international said. Leão described Osimhen’s decision as a reflection of the strong team spirit within the Galatasaray dressing room. “It’s about this kind of attitude. We have a great group, so I’m really happy to have this kind of teammates in the squad,” he added. He knows how much I struggled for that goal. I just want to give them back my quality and enjoy my game,” Leão said. Osimhen’s decision allowed Leão to convert the penalty and make it 4-0, capping a memorable evening for the Portuguese forward. The Nigerian striker’s contribution also made the occasion special, as he combined his goalscoring performance with a personal celebration following the arrival of his second daughter. The victory further strengthened Galatasaray’s position in the Turkish Super Lig as the club continues its domestic campaign under manager Okan Buruk.
